title: The Gnat and the Bull
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Gnat alighted on one of the horns of a Bull, and remained sitting there for a considerable time. When it had rested sufficiently and was about to fly away, it said to the Bull, "Do you mind if I go now?" The Bull merely raised his eyes and remarked, without interest, "It's all one to me; I didn't notice when you came, and I shan't know when you go away."
We may often be of more consequence in our own eyes than in the eyes of our neighbours.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Gnat land at the start?
options: On the Bull's back
On a nearby fence post
On one of the horns of a Bull
On the Bull's tail

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Gnat ask the Bull before flying away?
options: "Do you mind if I go now?"
"Did you feel me land on you?"
"May I rest here a while longer?"
"Have you noticed me at all?"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Bull respond to the Gnat's question?
options: He asks the Gnat to stay a little longer
He complains that the Gnat has bothered him
He thanks the Gnat for resting quietly
He remarks that it is all one to him, without interest

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Bull say about noticing the Gnat arrive?
options: That he saw the Gnat land immediately
That he didn't notice when the Gnat came
That he felt the Gnat's weight at once
That another animal told him about it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how long does the Gnat rest on the Bull's horn?
options: For only a moment
For the entire day
For a considerable time
Until nightfall

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Gnat bother to ask the Bull's permission before leaving?
options: It assumes its presence has been significant enough to matter to the Bull
It is worried the Bull might try to stop it
It wants to warn the Bull that it is leaving for good
It has been asked to check in with the Bull regularly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Bull's reply reveal about how he views the Gnat?
options: He was secretly annoyed by the Gnat the whole time
He had been waiting for the Gnat to leave
He respected the Gnat for resting so quietly
The Gnat's presence made no real difference to him at all

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Gnat "alighted" on the Bull's horn?
options: It crashed into it by accident
It landed and settled there
It circled around without landing
It was blown there by the wind

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Bull spoke "without interest"?
options: He spoke eagerly, wanting to know more
He spoke angrily, annoyed by the question
He spoke with no real concern about the matter
He spoke nervously, unsure how to answer

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: We can overestimate how much others notice or care about us
Bulls are less observant than most other animals
It is rude to ask permission before leaving somewhere
Small creatures should always avoid larger ones

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Gnat do once it has rested sufficiently?
options: It moves to the Bull's other horn
It begins buzzing loudly
It calls out to other gnats nearby
It prepares to fly away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Bull say he won't know?
options: Where the Gnat will go next
When the Gnat goes away
How long the Gnat has been resting
Why the Gnat chose his horn

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what part of his body does the Bull move when he answers?
options: His horns
His tail
His eyes
His ears

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is ironic about the Gnat asking permission to leave?
options: The Bull was never even aware the Gnat had arrived
The Bull had specifically invited the Gnat to stay
The Gnat had never actually landed on the Bull at all
The Bull had asked the Gnat to leave much earlier

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Bull's answer feel deflating to the Gnat's question?
options: It shows the Bull was frightened by the Gnat the whole time
It shows the Bull wanted the Gnat to stay longer
It shows the Bull had mistaken the Gnat for another animal
It shows the Gnat's presence mattered far less than the Gnat assumed

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "consequence" mean in the closing line?
options: Danger
Importance
Curiosity
Distance

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Bull asks a Gnat to leave its horn at once
A Gnat and a Bull become close companions
A Gnat learns its presence meant nothing to the Bull it rested on
A Bull thanks the Gnat for its company
